supernatural_elements: 提到诛灭提底之子的神（湿婆）

extraction_text: 优波曼纽为黑天举行加入苦行者行列的仪式。

details: 第三至第五个月仅食空气

extraction_text: 黑天苦行后看到天上出现灿烂光芒和异象。

attributes.description: 湿婆浑身金光，与妻子同在，因苦行、能量、美貌和光彩而辉煌

extraction_text: 黑天见到湿婆时感到震惊和敬畏。

attributes.description: 湿婆骑神牛，十一楼陀罗陪侍，众神唱赞歌

extraction_text: Numerous divine beings, including Indra, Vishnu, Aditi's two sons, and Brahma, sing the Rudra Tantra hymn before Shiva.
Countless yoga masters, gods, sages, celestial bodies, time units, directions, sacred knowledge, and all beings appear and bow to Shiva, the giver of yoga.
All beings, including animals and inanimate objects, worship Shiva with mind, speech, and action as the omnipotent lord Sarva appears before the narrator.
The narrator (Krishna) is unable to look directly at Shiva, so Shiva speaks first, telling Krishna to look up and speak.
Krishna bows in reverence to Shiva, pleasing Shiva's wife Uma, and then praises Shiva as the eternal origin of all existence.
The text describes the divine nature and attributes of a supreme being.

characters: Supreme Being (referred to with various epithets)
attributes.description: The being is described as the origin and dissolution of all beings, beyond sensory objects, mind, winds, fire, and celestial gods. Identified with the Vedas, sacrifice, Soma, Dakshina, sacrificial fire, and all ritual implements. The source of both virtues (sacrificial merit, generosity, Vedic study, restraint, modesty, fame, glory, satisfaction, success) and vices (desire, anger, fear, greed, pride, delusion, jealousy, sorrow, disease). Described as the cause of cosmic dissolution, the foremost entity, the inexhaustible source of all things, the birthplace of supreme intellect, the nature of existence, the eternal imperishable body, the unmanifest, the purifier, omnipresent, the thousand-rayed sun, the foremost among qualities, the sustainer of life, the great soul, thought, Brahman, the universe, compassion, the independent one, intelligence, wisdom, cognition, knowledge, understanding, will, and memory.
attributes.relationships: The being is the central reality upon which all beings, the world, intellect, and thought depend. Sages worship this being as the soul. The being pervades all places with arms, legs, eyes, heads, faces, and ears. It is the fruit of all actions performed in various units of time. It is the eternal light residing in the hearts of all beings. It is the final refuge of the wise.
attributes.supernatural_elements: Divine omnipresence, identification with cosmic principles and forces, source of all virtues and vices, eternal light, supreme reality.

extraction_text: The speaker addresses the being as 'Bhava, the remover of suffering' and concludes the discourse.

characters: Speaker (unidentified, possibly a sage or devotee)
Bhava (a name for the Supreme Being/Shiva)
attributes.description: The speaker concludes the philosophical discourse by addressing the supreme being as 'Bhava, the remover of suffering'. The text then notes that after these words were spoken to Bhava, the entire world, including animate and inanimate beings, let out a lion's roar.
attributes.relationships: The speaker is addressing Bhava. The narrative is being recounted to Yudhishthira (referred to as 'Prita's son').
attributes.supernatural_elements: The entire world's reaction (a lion's roar) to the conclusion of the discourse.

extraction_text: The text outlines the knowledge that leads to wisdom and union with the supreme being.

attributes.description: Learned Brahmins who understand these truths avoid sinking into ignorance. Those who know the being is steadfast, exists in the hearts of all beings, possesses infinite power, is the ancient Purusha, can assume infinite forms, shines like gold, and is the final refuge of the wise attain great or supreme wisdom. One who understands the seven subtle entities and the being's six characteristics, and practices yoga according to the fundamental rules, is wise and enters the being's great soul.
attributes.relationships: Learned Brahmins and sages understand and worship the being. Yogis, truth-seekers, and those who have mastered their senses depend on and take refuge in the being.
attributes.supernatural_elements: Knowledge leading to liberation from ignorance, entry into the divine soul through yoga.

extraction_text: Numerous divine beings, including gods, asuras, brahmins, nagas, pishachas, ancestors, birds, rakshasas, spirits, and great sages, all paid homage to the great god.
A fragrant rain of flowers fell from the sky onto Krishna's head, and a pleasant breeze blew.
Shankara (Shiva), the arranger of the world, looked at Goddess Uma, Krishna, and Indra, then spoke to Krishna.

attributes.relationships: Shiva is the great god; Uma is his consort; Krishna and Indra are addressed

extraction_text: Shiva acknowledged Krishna's devotion and offered him eight boons of his choice.

Krishna, overjoyed, bowed low to Shiva and requested eight boons: firm faith in dharma, victory in battle, highest honor, immense strength, dedication to yoga, constant closeness to Shiva, and hundreds of sons.
Shiva granted Krishna's requests.
Uma, the wife of Sharva (Shiva), mother of the world, spoke to Krishna and offered him eight boons from her.

attributes.relationships: Uma is Shiva's consort; she addresses Krishna

extraction_text: Krishna bowed to Uma and requested eight boons: not to anger the twice-born, his father's favor, a hundred sons, greatest happiness, love for family, his mother's favor, inner peace, and excellent abilities.
Uma granted the boons, promising Krishna 16,000 wives with mutual undying love, supreme love from his clan, handsome appearance, and daily meals for 7,000 guests in his home.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Divine promises of progeny, love, and prosperity

extraction_text: After granting the boons, Shiva and Uma disappeared instantly, followed by the other gods.
Krishna concludes by stating this is the marvelous story related to the brahmin Upamanyu, a man of superhuman energy.

attributes.relationships: Krishna narrates a story involving Upamanyu

extraction_text: Upamanyu pays homage to the God of Gods and addresses Krishna as 'Mausala'.
Upamanyu praises Shiva (Sharva) as the most generous in granting boons, strongest in battle, most exalted among gods, and whose abode is most desirable.
Upamanyu recounts the story of Sage Dandi who performed deep meditation (samadhi) for ten thousand years in the Krita Yuga to worship the Great God (Shiva).
Shiva was pleased with Sage Dandi's devotion and appeared before him.
Sage Dandi praised Shiva with various hymns, calling him the purest among the pure, the highest path among all paths, the most powerful energy, and the highest austerity.
Sage Dandi states that Shiva is worshipped by Gandharvas, Asuras, and Indra, and is the giver of liberation to ascetics who fear the suffering of birth and death.
Sage Dandi declares that even Brahma, Vishnu, gods, and sages cannot comprehend Shiva's true nature, and that everything in the world originates from and depends on Shiva.
Sage Dandi explains that Shiva is one god with three forms (Trimurti) and has various supreme aspects including Atipurusha, Atiatma, Atipreta, Atidevata, Atiloka, Ativijñana, and Atiyajña.
Sage Dandi states that wise people who recognize Shiva within all beings attain liberation, while those who don't recognize him remain trapped in the cycle of rebirth.

Sage Dandi identifies Shiva as being all things including liberation, heaven, desire, anger, goodness, sorrow, darkness, lower worlds, upper worlds, various gods, elements, senses, and both existence and non-existence.
The speaker expresses realization of attaining the ultimate goal that only the most virtuous can achieve through knowledge and purity.
The speaker acknowledges past ignorance and lack of awareness, contrasting with the wise who recognize the divine as supreme and eternal.
After many lifetimes, the speaker gains the opportunity to see the divine directly, noting divine favor toward devotees and the promise of immortality for those who recognize divine greatness.

extraction_text: Dandi, a great ascetic, offered praises to the immortal Ishana (Shiva) and sang about the supreme Brahman.
Shiva, pleased with the praises, told Dandi that even Brahma, Indra (Sakra), Vishnu, and all gods and great sages do not know him.
Shiva granted Dandi immortality, freedom from suffering, abundant energy, good reputation, and divine knowledge.
Shiva promised that sages would visit Dandi and that his son would become a scripture author due to Shiva's grace.
Shiva asked Dandi what else he desired and offered to fulfill it that day.
Dandi requested that his faith in Shiva remain forever firm.
Shiva granted Dandi's request and then disappeared amid the assembly's admiration.
After Shiva and the accompanying gods left, Dandi came to the narrator's hermitage and recounted these events.
The narrator mentions that Brahma spoke of 10,000 names of Shiva in the Vedas, and their scriptures mention 1,000 names.
Dandi knew Shiva's generally secret names due to Brahma's favor.
